title: Why sunsets are red and orange
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why is the sky red at sunset?
Why does the Sun look orange when it sets?
Why are some sunsets extra red?

explain.say: Sunlight is a mix of all colours. As it passes through air, tiny air molecules scatter blue light much more than red, which is why the daytime sky is blue.

explain.say: At midday the Sun is high, so its light takes a short path through the air. Only a little blue is scattered away and the Sun looks white-yellow.

explain.say: At sunset the Sun is low, so its light crosses up to about forty times more air. Almost all the blue and green is scattered out along the way, leaving red and orange.

explain.say: That red light paints the clouds and sky. Dust, smoke or ash from volcanoes high in the air can make sunsets even deeper red.

faq.q: Why is the sky red at sunset?
faq.a: When the Sun is low, its light travels through much more air to reach you. Air scatters blue light away along the way, so mostly red and orange light is left to colour the sky.
Rayleigh scattering is the way tiny particles like air molecules scatter short-wave blue light much more strongly than long-wave red light. It makes the day sky blue and sunsets red.
asks: Why does air scatter blue light?
What scatters light in the sky?

faq.q: Why does the Sun look orange when it sets?
faq.a: The light coming straight from the low Sun has lost most of its blue and green on its long trip through the air. What remains is yellow, orange and red.
asks: Why is the setting Sun red?

faq.q: Why are some sunsets extra red?
faq.a: Extra particles high in the air, such as volcanic ash, wildfire smoke or dust, scatter and absorb even more blue light. After big eruptions, sunsets around the world can be deep red for months.
asks: Why do volcanoes make red sunsets?
Why was the sunset so bright tonight?

faq.q: Is the sky red at sunset on Mars too?
faq.a: No, it is the opposite. On Mars fine dust scatters red light across the day sky, but near the setting Sun the sky looks bluish.
asks: What colour is a sunset on Mars?

facts: Air molecules scatter blue light several times more strongly than red light, an effect called Rayleigh scattering.
When the Sun is on the horizon, its light passes through roughly 38 times as much air as when it is directly overhead.
